result.title: What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability
result.summary: The corner of a box or a room, where three perpendicular edges meet, appears in an image as three segments meeting at a point. We ask what such junctions reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsic parameters. Each junction is consistent with an explicit convex set of cameras; when only the focal length is unknown, this set is an interval in closed form. These sets are computed from the image alone, so calibrating from many junctions is a convex feasibility problem. Almost every junction bounds the focal length from below; we characterize when one also bounds it from above, and when many junctions determine it exactly. For a known vertex, the bounds can be certified against any bounded error in the measured edge directions.

AI.brief_summary: 研究图像中三垂直棱边交点（如箱角、房间角）对未标定相机内参的约束：每个交点对应一个显式凸相机集合，仅焦距未知时该集合为闭式区间，并刻画何时给出焦距上界、何时多个交点可唯一确定焦距，以及在棱边方向存在有界误差时的可认证界。
AI.relevance_reason: 其几何参数可辨识性与认证界的分析，可能为判断视觉表示中任务必要的几何信息能否从证据唯一恢复、以及如何给出不确定性界限提供概念参照，可供核查是否用于 LVR 的视觉证据筛选与可信度评估。
